description: Source of truth for which artwork has been confirmed and assigned. artwork/ itself is gitignored (bulk, large); this file is tracked, so it's the only durable record that an assignment happened. Check this before assigning anything new -- the same picture must never get used for two things. A `kind: "npc"` entry's `ref` is the character's canonical id (matching its ideas/story/bible/characters/<id>.md filename stem where one exists) -- it will NOT resolve against data/npcs/*.json for any character that hasn't been promoted to a real NPC file yet (Shucks Mordant, Hyuck, Rupiah and Anabala all currently have none). That's expected, not a bug: the portrait exists and is assigned before the data file does. Scene-brief cast ids are kept aligned to this same canonical id where practical (episode-c1s1--intake-medicals.json's Shucks cast entry was renamed shucks -> shucks-mordant 2026-09-09 for exactly this reason).

assets.note: An elevated coastal highway curving toward the city skyline, dramatic cumulus cloud bank, warm evening light. The road the six spotlights of The Road In are each travelling, from a distance.

Already named by the artist -- a skeletal figure in a white coat and stethoscope, arms folded, standing in a cluttered clinic office with a wall clock and a first-aid kit. Matches the bible's doctor-founder exactly.
Companion detail shot -- his skeletal hand resting on a desk edge, warm side light. A close-up variant, not the primary portrait.

Already named by the artist -- a massive gnoll warrior, feathers and painted bands, low-angle heroic framing. Confirms the gnoll-statue connection: Hyuck himself is the gnoll. Founder, alongside Shucks Mordant and Rupiah (blank-inheritance-master-timeline.md, ~200 years ago).

Already named by the artist -- an elf-eared figure in golden window light, moths nearby, contemplative profile. The third founder alongside Hyuck and Shucks Mordant. Confirmed 2026-09-10 (LEDGER.md #8): elf, elf nobility specifically -- the portrait's reading was accurate.

Already named by the artist, found under character-portraits/mitflits/ -- blue-skinned, tall-eared, wide-brimmed hat and round tinted glasses. The mitflit founder who recruited Hyuck, Shucks Mordant and Rupiah to intervene ~200 years ago (mitflits.md already names her as the founder).

A spacious dining hall, tall windows with tree light, rows of wooden tables and chairs, papers stacked on side counters. Matches 'a room built for hundreds' -- picked as primary over canteen_02 (more classroom-like, kept as an alternate).
Alternate angle -- reads more like a classroom/study hall (chalkboard visible) than a dining hall. Kept as a secondary variant, not the primary.
An institutional waiting room, rows of bench seating, notices pinned to a peeling wall, a wall clock. Matches 'the medical hall, first morning' -- The Queue beat.
A real examination room -- gurney, equipment, city view through blinds. This is specifically Shucks's own room for the 'one at a time' private beat, pairs with his portrait.
Quartermaster's stores -- shelving of gear, a pegboard of tools, jackets on hooks, red storage crates. Matches Kit Issue's counter/stores exactly.
A vaulted underground chamber, ankle-deep sludge lit green, a control panel and archway at the back. Primary image for the compactor chamber itself.
A large cylindrical generator/turbine with a control panel beside it. Matches the 'power-the-line' basic check specifically -- an adjacent room to the main chamber.
Another industrial machine bay, radiators and a press, a green door at the back. Third variant/detail shot for the same underground complex.

A brick building entrance, stone steps, lit doorway among trees. NOT tied to one specific scene brief -- general Directorate facility exterior. No dedicated bible/locations/directorate-headquarters.md exists yet; flagged for the user rather than assumed onto a specific scene.
An industrial roller-shutter loading entrance, cluttered storefront-style stockroom, a vending machine outside. Same caveat as the exterior shot -- general facility image, not scene-specific.
An interior corridor/lobby -- double doors, bookshelves, a noticeboard, a wall clock. Same caveat -- general facility interior, not scene-specific.

The campaign's own overture. Reserved out of the (otherwise empty) moment-of-cool pool so it can never turn up at random -- it plays exactly once, cold-opening 'The Road In', and nowhere else. See data/audio/soundscapes/episode-c1s1--the-road-in.json.

'Section Nine's first blood' -- the campaign's very first fight (six Giant Centipedes, c1s1-flood-tunnel) gets a track of its own rather than a shuffle from the 27-track battle pool, on Ingram's own instruction to reserve specific songs for specific events. Title translates roughly to '<a name>'s Appearance/Entrance' -- fits creatures erupting out of the sludge better than anything generic. Bound as both the soundscape's combat.track (if a real Foundry Combat is tracked) and a dedicated cue on the 'the-fight' beat (fires with zero Foundry combat setup, which is the more reliable path for a scene run straight off the Scene Runner).

Reserved for the cicada-stencil mystery thread (ideas/entries/cicada-motif.json) -- NOT used as a music cue in Session 0/1 itself (see data/audio/cues/cicada-motif-appears.json, which uses only a quiet ambience layer so nothing has to explain what music to return to afterward). Reserved now, ahead of use, so it can never be discovered by a future GM already sitting in the mystery pool's shuffle before this thread deserves its own cue -- the actual musical moment is future work.

A wooden shopfront under a huge tree, flowers in pots down the steps, deep summer light. The hero image for The Errand -- the quarter around The General Store, and the Tea House a few doors down that takes messages for the old man.
Inside the tea house. Where a message for him is left, and where at least one player leaves with a way to reach him again.

An alley wall carrying the cicada stencil. Cut to this for the-mark-again beat; the audio cue of the same name slips a real cicada drone into the ambience under it (data/audio/cues/cicada-motif-appears.json). Deliberately NOT scored as ominous -- see design/audio-system.md 11.
A monumental brutalist atrium -- curved concrete piers, a spiral stair, two tiny figures for scale. The Directorate at its most impersonal; general facility image, not scene-specific.
